text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT (sev2) — GPU autoscaling failing in us-west1. inference-queue-gpu backlog growing, HPA not scaling (custom metrics adapter returning 503s). Alerting oncall.

alice.m: paging @ben.platform and @cindy-ml — seeing queue length spike on inference-gpu (>750), autoscaler not kicking. Some requests are being throttled with 429.

ben.platform: on it. pulled prometheus-adapter logs, seeing timeouts and 503s to prometheus-k8s api. maybe metrics-adapter out of resources or queue backlog. grabbing kubectl now.

cindy-ml: adding context — batcher backlog increases token latency and causes long-lived KV cache entries, so once GPUs are saturated throughput drops and queue explodes. If autoscale doesn't react we risk regional capacity exhaustion.

alice.m: severity classified sev2 since customer-facing errors visible. Support getting tickets. Sam, can you confirm any customers impacted?

sam-support: opening high-priority support tickets for any 5xx/429s. Early list: tenant acme-corp (client-prod-usw1), tenant-bravo (ml-saas). Flagging for SLA watchers. Ticket IDs: INC-17902, INC-17903.

ben.platform: running quick checks:
```
kubectl get hpa -n prod inference-gpu
NAME            REFERENCE                TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-gpu   Deployment/inference    0%/60%     2         16        2          7d
```
HPA reports 0% target because custom metric not returning.

ben.platform: describe metrics adapter pod shows repeated 503s talking to prometheus:
```
kubectl logs prometheus-adapter-0 -n monitoring
ERROR: failed to query prometheus: 503 Service Unavailable
```
Suggesting prometheus or network between adapter and prometheus is failing.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline for prometheus-adapter shows a restart ~5m ago (image pull ok). No recent config pushes.

alice.m: quick mitigation options: 1) manual scale inference-gpu to handle surge 2) restart prometheus-adapter pod(s) 3) failover traffic to cpu-backed pool or hosted fallback. Which order?

ben.platform: doing manual scale first to stop throttles.

ben.platform: `kubectl scale deploy inference-gpu -n prod --replicas=10` — scaled to 10 replicas. Watch queue.

alice.m: confirm scaling helped?

cindy-ml: monitoring queue length — immediate drop in queued requests from ~780 -> ~220 over 60s. Latency p95 dropping from ~12s -> ~6s. Errors still present but reduced.

sam-support: customers still seeing intermittent 429s for next 2 minutes, but overall error rate dropping. Sending customer updates: "We are mitigating increased latency; temporary capacity increase applied; engineering investigating autoscaling."

ben.platform: next action: restart prometheus-adapter pods to restore metric flow to HPA. Doing rolling restart.

ben.platform: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter -n monitoring`

deploy-bot: rollout started for prometheus-adapter — 3 replicas. Healthchecks enabled.

ben.platform: watching adapter logs — new pods start and begin scraping. Initial queries succeed. HPA metrics readouts returning.

alice.m: good. after adapter healthy we should let HPA manage downscaling to avoid excess cost. Set a conservative cooldown.

cindy-ml: also adding a protective rule: temporarily raise HPA minReplicas to 4 to avoid thrash while adapter stabilizes.

ben.platform: applied `kubectl patch hpa inference-gpu -n prod -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 4}}'` — minReplicas=4.

oncall-sre-bot: NOTE: autoscaler observed and will resume once metrics stable. If adapter fails again, fallback policy: route 20% of new traffic to cpu-pool in us-west1.

alice.m: can we enable fallback now to reduce customer pain?

ben.platform: enabling traffic split to cpu-pool via router: `rwctl route set inference-service --split us-west1:80,us-west1-cpu:20` — commit ID a1b2c3.

sam-support: sending updated message to affected customers: short outage window, mitigations applied, ETA for full resolution 30m.

cindy-ml: root cause hypothesis: prometheus ingestion flapped (high cardinality spike from a noisy job), adapter overloaded and returned 503s — HPA lost visibility. Need to confirm prometheus scrape and retention.

ben.platform: digging into prometheus: `curl -s http://prometheus-k8s.monitoring.svc:9090/-/ready` returns 200 but query latency high. There's a spike in series churn from job `workload-metrics/finetune-run-*/metrics`. I'm going to temporarily block that job's high-cardinality label to reduce query cost.

alice.m: do it. patch scrape config to drop high-card labels from that job. Also schedule a follow-up to tune recording rules / relabeling.

ben.platform: patched Prometheus scrape relabel config for `workload-metrics` to drop `run_id` label. Reloaded config. Query p95 for adapter -> prometheus back to normal.

cindy-ml: recommend longer-term: add aggregation recording rules and rate-limit noisy tenants, also add alerting on prometheus query latency for adapter queries.

sam-support: customer update: Prometheus adapter restart + capacity increase reduced visible errors. We'll keep customers updated.

alice.m: status check: queue back to normal ~40, p95 ~2000ms, HPA replicas currently 6. Observability shows adapter metrics healthy for 7m.

ben.platform: marking incident mitigated. Next steps: postmortem, include timeline, root cause (high-card scrape caused adapter overload), fix plan: relabel, recording rules, autoscaler fallback improvements, automated adapter restarts on 5xx > threshold.

oncall-sre-bot: Incident moved to MITIGATED. Please file postmortem and link to this thread.

alice.m: I'll own the postmortem. tagging @cindy-ml for model/batcher impact notes, @ben.platform for infra changes.

sam-support: will follow up with customer comms.

ben.platform: handing off to night oncall @oncall-night in case adapter or prometheus flaps again. Handoff notes: adapter restart done, prom relabel applied, hpa minReplicas=4, traffic split set (20% cpu fallback), manual scale removed and HPA control returned.

oncall-sre-bot: Handoff acknowledged. Night oncall: monitor adapter 5xx and HPA readouts for next 2 hours.

alice.m: thanks team. postmortem drafted and will link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
